title: Find Peak Element
description:
A **peak element** is an element that is strictly greater than its neighbors.

Given a 0-indexed integer array `nums`, find a peak element and return its 0-based index. If the array contains multiple peaks, return the index to **any** of the peaks.

You may imagine that `nums[-1] = nums[n] = -infinity`. In other words, an element is always considered strictly greater than a neighbor that is outside the array.

You must write an algorithm that runs in `O(log n)` time. The judge validates that your returned index is in bounds and is a valid peak (`true`).
constraints: nums[i] != nums[i + 1] for all valid i.
hints: Because adjacent elements are never equal and the boundaries are treated as -infinity, every non-empty array is guaranteed to contain at least one peak.
At any midpoint mid, compare nums[mid] with nums[mid + 1]: if nums[mid] < nums[mid + 1], the slope rises to the right, so a peak must exist in [mid + 1, right].
Otherwise nums[mid] > nums[mid + 1], meaning a peak must exist in [left, mid]. Repeat until left == right.

examples.explanation: Index 2 (value 3) is a peak element because 3 > 2 and 3 > 1.
Both index 1 (value 2) and index 5 (value 6) are valid peaks; returning either index passes validation.
A single-element array has its only peak at index 0.

inputs.name: nums
inputs.description: Array of integers where adjacent values differ
